query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and is intended to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance in its solidified solid-solution state, but its dynamic behavior across different temperatures and strain rates lacks a theoretical explanation. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could account for this behavior, and what controlled comparison within that regime would distinguish it? Specify predictions relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and a falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The elimination of Co from the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy raises the effective stacking fault energy (SFE) of the resulting Co‐free FeNiCrMn alloy. This increased SFE suppresses strain‐induced twinning and shifts the dominant deformation mechanism toward dislocation glide. Consequently, the dynamic mechanical response (i.e. the strain-rate and temperature dependence of the strength–ductility balance) will differ from that of the baseline equiatomic alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: A solidified, single-phase FCC solid solution of Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy prepared from the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi composition by removing Co.
generation.intervention: Removal of Co from the equiatomic alloy (i.e. comparing the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy with the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy baseline).
generation.conditions: Uniaxial tensile testing will be conducted over a matrix of strain rates (ranging from quasi‐static to high dynamic rates) and temperatures (from room temperature to intermediate elevated temperatures where the FCC phase remains stable). All controlled variables (e.g. sample dimensions, solidification route, and testing environment) are held constant aside from the alloy composition.
generation.structural_mediator: Effective stacking fault energy (SFE) which governs the relative activation of deformation twinning versus dislocation glide.
generation.mechanism: The removal of Co increases the effective SFE of the alloy. A higher SFE suppresses the nucleation of deformation twins and favors dislocation glide. Under dynamic loading, this mechanism alters the strain-rate sensitivity and temperature dependence of the material’s yield strength and work hardening, thereby affecting the overall strength–ductility balance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy, the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy will exhibit (a) a lower density of deformation twins (as verified by microstructural examination) and (b) a modified yield strength and strain-rate sensitivity profile—potentially showing higher yield strength at higher strain rates due to enhanced dislocation-mediated hardening.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy, which typically has a lower SFE that promotes deformation twinning under dynamic conditions.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies within the FCC phase stability regime, for samples processed into homogeneous solid-solution states and deformed under controlled uniaxial tensile loading at strain rates ranging from quasi‑static up to high dynamic rates and at temperatures where no phase transformations occur.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative change in SFE due to Co removal and the precise magnitude of its impact on dislocation mobility and strain rate sensitivity remains uncertain until directly measured or computed.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloys – one being the Co‑free FeNiCrMn alloy and the other the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy – under identical processing conditions. Subject both compositions to uniaxial tensile tests across a series of strain rates (e.g., 10⁻³, 10⁻¹, and 10³ s⁻¹) and at various temperatures in the FCC stability range. In addition to recording stress-strain data, perform microstructural analyses (using TEM and/or EBSD) to quantify the density of deformation twins versus dislocation structures, and (if possible) assess the local SFE by diffraction or ab initio methods.
measurements: Stress–strain curves to extract yield strength, strain-rate sensitivity, and work-hardening rates
Microstructural characterization (e.g., twin density, dislocation arrangements) via TEM/EBSD
Direct or computed estimates of the material’s stacking fault energy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy does not display a statistically significant reduction in deformation twinning, or if its yield strength and strain-rate sensitivity profiles are not measurably different from (or inferior to) those of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy under the same testing conditions, then the hypothesis that higher SFE (from Co removal) controls the dynamic behavior is falsified.
